messages:
alisha: FYI — we're seeing a big spike in preemptions on the us-west1 spot GPU pool over the last 15m. Jobs failing with OOM or node loss.
marco: Seen it. Autoscaler didn't spin up fallback on-demand nodes fast enough; several batches queued. Any alert firing?
infra-bot: [ALERT] gke-us-west1-spot-gpu: spot interruption rate 18% (threshold 10%) — 15m average.
sasha: kubectl top nodes looks noisy. sample:
```
NAME                                      CPU(cores)   MEMORY(bytes)
gpu-spot-7x8k   1200m        16Gi
gpu-on-demand-2  100m         1Gi
```
We also saw a bunch of NotReady soon after interruptions.
alisha: Root cause guess: cloud-side preemption wave + our autoscaler scale-up-delay defaults (60s) + expander strategy preferring largest pool (spot) -> slow fallback.
tom: Can we adjust cluster-autoscaler config: reduce scale-up-delay, enable warm-pool for on-demand fallback, and change expander to least-waste? Also we can increase fallback pool min size.
priya: Cost tradeoff: increasing on-demand standby will raise baseline cost ~+12% but reduces job retries. We should quantify by workload.
marco: Quick fix: create a small hot-standby node pool with 2 on-demand GPUs labelled gpu.hot-standby and set a nodeSelector/priorityClass for batch jobs. I'll push a YAML.
marco: YAML snippet:
```
apiVersion: container.cnrm.cloud.google.com/v1beta1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: gpu-hot-standby
spec:
  autoscaling:
    minNodeCount: 2
    maxNodeCount: 2
  management:
    autoRepair: true
  nodeConfig:
    machineType: n1-standard-8
    accelerators:
    - type: nvidia-tesla-t4
      count: 1
    labels:
      pool: gpu-hot-standby
```
alisha: Also set taint `gpu-hot-standby=true:NoSchedule` and let batch job pods tolerate it. That keeps standby reserved for heavy jobs.
sasha: We'll also add a cluster-autoscaler flag `--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false` and reduce `--scale-up-delay=10s` in k8s CA deployment.
priya: Agree. Action items: marco to create pool + taint (ETA 30m), sasha to update CA flags (ETA 1h), tom to run cost baseline by EOD. Alisha to notify ops and follow up.
alisha: If interruptions continue after hot-standby, we'll consider temporary capacity reservation or switching traffic to other regions (us-central) as fallback.
infra-bot: Incident recorded: #INC-2026-032 us-west1 spot churn. Assigned: marco, sasha, tom.
